jobs.title: Videographer, Scout Studios
jobs.description_text: Overview Scout Studios is looking for a versatile Videographer who can move quickly, think visually, and take a story from idea to finish. You'll help own the high-volume brand content pipeline that surrounds Scout's flagship storytelling, adding depth and character to the company’s story by capturing the people, vehicles, events, moments, and stories inside Scout Motors as the company continues to build. One week you may be shooting a walkthrough at the Scout Motors Production Center in Blythewood, SC, the next, producing an experiential event recap, filming a product walkaround, supporting a CRM story, or off-roading in the desert, producing product development and adventure stories. This role will be deeply embedded in the ongoing development of the Scout Motors company, brand, and vehicles, and is poised to own the content work that is quick, nimble, culturally aware, and often the most frequent interaction our audience will have with the Scout brand on our content channels. You'll collaborate with the broader Scout Studios team while working directly with the Head of Scout Studios to develop a content and storytelling pipeline and creative identity of your own. Why Scout Studios Scout Motors and the Scout brand have a rare and special opportunity: we're building the company, the vehicles, the community, and the stories surrounding them from the ground up, at the same time. jobs.company: The Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence
jobs.title: Research Engineer, Robotics - Roboticist
jobs.description_text: If you have questions about on-site work arrangements for this role, please ask your recruiter. Our base salary range is $128,880 - $193,320, and in addition we have generous bonus plans to provide a competitive compensation package. Who You Are: You will own the control stack on our physical robots and the path from simulation to them. This is first and foremost a controls role: you will bring up and tune real-time, torque-level control on arms, multi-fingered hands, bimanual systems and humanoids, make it stable and safe enough that researchers run experiments on hardware every day, and build the interfaces that learned policies plug into. Experience with humanoid whole-body control and with Unitree platforms (G1, H1 and similar) is a strong plus, as humanoid and whole-body work is a growing share of the lab. You will also design and build the hardware the research needs, from end-effectors to test rigs. You will work closely with research scientists and the simulation team so that what is learned in simulation shows up as reliable behaviour on hardware. Who We Are: The Robotics team at Ai2, led by Dieter Fox, uses scalable simulation to study how foundation models scale and generalize for robotics. We focus on manipulation, humanoid and whole-body control, large-scale simulated training, sim-to-real transfer, robot foundation models and skill learning. We publish at CoRL, ICRA, RSS, CVPR, NeurIPS, ICLR and ICML, and everything we build is open source. Your Next Challenge:

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Data Governance & Trust
jobs.description_text: Staff Software Engineer, Data Governance & Trust San Mateo, CA About the role Sony Interactive Entertainment is seeking a Staff Software Engineer to help shape and deliver the technical foundation for Data Governance and Trust across our data and AI ecosystem. Our ambition is to make data understandable, reliable, reusable, and appropriately governed for the people, applications, and AI systems that depend on it. Achieving this requires shared platform capabilities, clear ownership, and governance practices embedded into how teams build and operate data products. In this role, you will establish technical direction, lead initiatives across teams, and remain hands-on in architecture and implementation. You will connect metadata, lineage, data quality, semantic context, and policy controls into practical capabilities that help teams use data with confidence. You will also be a trusted technical representative for the Data Governance and Trust group. We are looking for someone who can lead productive discussions, explain complex tradeoffs, navigate difficult conversations, and build alignment across engineering, business, governance, security, and privacy stakeholders. This is an individual contributor leadership role with impact across teams. What you will do Set technical direction and deliver shared capabilities Shape the architecture and technical roadmap for Data Governance and Trust in partnership with engineering leadership, product partners, domain teams, and governance

jobs.description_text: Meet the team Torc’s Perception teams develop the production machine learning systems that enable our autonomous trucks to understand their surroundings. These systems must run in real-time on embedded compute while remaining robust to adverse weather, sensor degradation, and sensor failures. The team works across machine learning, 3D perception, and embedded systems, balancing perception performance and robustness against latency, memory, power and on-board compute budget. You will collaborate closely with teams across sensor hardware, data, infrastructure, simulation, compute platform, systems engineering, safety, perception, and planning. jobs.description_text: Meet the Team The Senior Autonomy Core Frameworks Software Engineer plays a critical role in architecting and advancing the foundational frameworks that underpin Torc's autonomous driving stack. This role helps in owning technical direction for the software in core autonomy components, helping to raise the bar on code quality, and driving improvements across the autonomy software. As a senior technical leader, you will collaborate closely with the Behavior and Perception teams within Autonomy to design robust, composable architectural patterns that serve as the foundation for safe, performant, reliable autonomous operation. This position demands deep technical expertise in software architecture and autonomous vehicle fundamentals. What You’ll Do Lead the architecture, design, implementation, and evolution of core frameworks that serve as the foundation for Torc's autonomous driving stack, including state management, inter-component communication, abstraction layers, and common utilities used across all software systems. Drive the technical direction for real-time C++ architectural components and patterns responsible for reliable system-wide data flow, component coordination, error handling, and operational observability. jobs.description_text: Meet the Team The Mission Interface Software Engineer plays a key role in delivering Vehicle Intent software into the automated driving system at Torc. This role focuses on developing high-quality, production-ready software that enables our Mission Control and Remote Assistance teams to interact with the self-driving truck’s software stack capabilities. In this position, you are expected to demonstrate technical leadership, operate with a high degree of autonomy, and drive cross-team initiatives across software, systems, and product domains. The software developed in this role directly enables communication with and command over our vehicles to sense their surroundings, respond intelligently when necessary, and help keep the system operating safely — advancing Torc’s mission to commercialize self-driving trucks for safe, sustained, long-haul innovation in the freight industry. jobs.title: Test and Launch Engineer II - Vehicle
jobs.description_text: NEUTRON Neutron is a medium-lift launch vehicle being developed by Rocket Lab, a publicly traded end-to-end space company. The rocket can deliver the mega constellations of tomorrow, enable interplanetary payloads, and support human spaceflight. As a reusable platform, Neutron will deliver a very cost-effective and reliable launch solution leveraging Rocket Lab's proven history with Electron – the second most launched rocket, worldwide, in 2024. If you're interested in joining an incredible team in a fast-paced and rewarding environment, this is your opportunity. HASTE HASTE (Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron) is a specialized variant of Rocket Lab's proven Electron launch vehicle, designed to support hypersonic flight testing and research missions. Operating from Rocket Lab's Launch Complex 2 at Wallops Island, Virginia, Electron HASTE provides a unique capability to deliver hypersonic test vehicles to the required flight conditions for cutting-edge aerodynamic and propulsion research. The program represents an exciting evolution of the Electron platform, supporting critical national defense and aerospace research objectives while maintaining Rocket Lab's commitment to rapid, reliable launch operations.
